text: The DP-added H and C dependencies are platform wave-0 contracts and published contracts that this APP story builds against as fakes; none blocks the build, so Depends on (build) stays None and Ready to start stays Day 1.
why: R5.5 adds the dependencies and R5.7 rules 2 and 8 say a CON or a published contract never blocks an APP story; the metadata carries only the legacy-key contract dependency, and the story must still be able to start on Day 1.
read: Template and Rules R5.5 rows DP-03, DP-04, DP-06, DP-07, DP-10, DP-14, DP-15 and DP-19; R5.7 rules 2 and 8; RWB-P3-E2042-CON.
confirm: Solution architect at the contract review
impact: No date, wave or lane change; the fakes are the build path until the platform contracts and the P3 contracts land.

text: This story copies the label of its own legacy key, PMT-2026.12 with valid from 2026-12-15, and does not adopt PM-2026.12 or 2026-12-01; the two are reconciled to one version row before SIT.
why: R7.3 takes the legacy story first and R-PREC does not rank RWB-E2-027 above this key for this value; choosing the other label silently would change a value the legacy approver signed off.
read: Legacy RWB-E2-042 section 3; the RWB-E2-027 lineage as carried by RWB-P7-E2027-APP; R7.3 fill order.
confirm: Business analyst and the owner of RWB-E2-027 before SIT
impact: The registry may hold one package with two labels until the reconciliation; the tests use PMT-2026.12 and do not assert the other label.

text: The decision code of a governance record is resolved at run time from the LOV-DECISION list read through DP-07, and no literal code is written in the story, the code or the tests.
why: DF-DEC-003 requires a LOV value and the list is reference data owned by P3, so a code in code would be an ungoverned business value and would break when the list version changes.
read: TSD P7 v2 T3.1 DF-DEC-003 and T3.2; FSD P7 v3 A2.7; Template and Rules R7.3.
confirm: Decision log owner and the LOV-DECISION owner
impact: The tests assert the presence of a code from the list, not a literal value; a list version change needs no build.

text: The database login is written only as 'the rwb-decision login (DP-02)', and its name is left to the platform DB story that creates the login and the grants.
why: DP-02 fixes one login per service but no source names it; the monolith login must not be reused, and inventing a name would be a fabricated credential identifier.
read: Template and Rules R4 and R5.5 DP-02; Architecture v5 slide 29 grants model.
impact: No test depends on the login string; the migration and the application role are provisioned from the platform secret store.

text: The MSG-P3-027 detail for the two Epic 2 checks names rule IDs, row orders and column names only, never a case fact, a customer or a person, and the check value stays 'schema' for both.
why: The legacy story places both checks inside the schema check and restricts the detail to row IDs and cells; without a fixed naming rule two implementations would produce different refusals for the same workbook.
read: Legacy RWB-E2-042 sections 5 and 14; FSD P7 v3 A2.7 AC-EXC-P7-007-02.
impact: The refusal text is stable across services and carries no personal data; the exact wording may be revised once without changing the check.

text: The four registry tables and decision_log_entry are P7's in rwb_decision under the R-PREC default ruling and ASM-A6-tables-3; the P3 and P4 declarations of the same tables are not built and no foreign key crosses a schema.
why: Architecture v5 slides 27 and 41 and the R-PREC default ruling put governance in rwb-decision, and the Ownership Map records the reading; TSD P4 v3 and TSD P3 v3 predate that ruling.
read: Architecture v5 slides 27 and 41; R-PREC default ruling (Template and Rules R3); Ownership Map v1 rule_package, rule_package_version, rule_row and rule_test_case; ASM-A6-tables-3.
confirm: Solution architect; the P7 TSD owner at its next version
impact: This story owns the tables and no other service reads them; the P3 and P4 stories read them only through the P7 operations, and the P7 TSD needs an update.

text: Defaults for the unspecified values: the seed writes the package code as the title until RW-COE supplies one; the dry-run counts are stored and served but their breakdown is asserted for presence and stability only; MSG-P3-015 is reported by its message ID with the text left to its owner; the rollback answer carries the two version states and the reason; with the legacy flag off the three admin operations answer as unavailable and the registry stays readable.
why: The story cannot be built or tested without a shape for these values, and inventing a title, a business count or a message text would put a fabricated value in the registry or in a message catalogue.
read: Legacy RWB-E2-042 sections 12 to 14; FSD P7 v3 A2.7; TSD P7 v2 T3.1.
applied_in: 7 AC1 and AC4; 11 Data; 12.1; 13 Solution plan; 14 Validation and messages
confirm: Business analyst, RW-COE and the message catalogue owner before SIT
impact: No business number is asserted by a test; each default is replaced by the confirmed value without a schema change.

text: The traceability table cites Epic 1 section 4 and Program section 5.3 for REQ-CWC-013 and REQ-CWC-014, keeps the requirement IDs and text unchanged, and notes the stale legacy pointer to Epic 1 3.3 and Epic 2 3.2/3.8.
why: BRD Epic 1 v4 and Program v4 carry the requirement set, while the legacy pointer predates the BRD v2 and v4 structure; a silent change would hide a stale reference and a silent copy would point at the wrong section.
read: Business Requirements Epic 1 v4 section 4; Business Requirements Epic 2 v2 sections 3.1 to 3.10; Business Requirements Program v4 section 5.3.
impact: Traceability points at the right sections and the requirement text is unchanged; no requirement ID moves.
